src: Detroit News, 15 Jul 1880, p. 2, 'Finding of the Hidden Treasure of the Chief Wabasis' (from the Greenville Daily Bee; Newspapers.com 1377553520): earliest print
tw-mi-wabasis-lake-gold.st: The 1880 telling (earliest print found): the chief received about $10,000 at Grand Rapids for tribal lands, put it in a strong box and sank it in Wahnoketo (Wabasis) Lake; he was killed for it and his bones later found on the shore; 'no trace of the treasure'. The paper's sequel of a man digging up an oak coffer of gold is a comic tall tale, not a find.

src: Illinois State Register, 3 Oct 1942, p. 1, 'Dispute Over Buried Wealth Goes to Court' (AP Eureka; Newspapers.com 1325120320)
tw-il-eureka-onnen-henhouse.st: By Oct 1942 eight fruit jars had been recovered, one with $6,400 in bills and seven with $175-200 each in quarters and halves, plus about $3,000 in an old trunk; the bills went to eight nieces and nephews, the silver and trunk money to two sisters, and an accounting suit followed. The coin collection was not among the finds reported.
